chapter: Later road work and the jazz tradition
title: Playing New Orleans with Eddie Haywood and Butterbeans and Susie
summary: He last played New Orleans on drums in Eddie Haywood's band with Butterbeans and Susie, around 1931.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Oh, I was going to ask, you mentioned once you were down in New Orleans a few months or a couple of months and played there, did you?

the last, the last time that I played there, I played with Butter Beans and Susie Shaw. Oh, yeah. Old man, Eddie Haywood, had the band and I was playing drums and all. See, I doubled on drums too. Oh,

Yeah, and I was playing drums in the orchestra with Eddie Haywood and we had trumpet and sax. We'd always carry along and then we'd, in the towns like New Orleans, another place where we'd rather increase our band than we'd add those extra men to it. We kept the four regular with us like that. And so, we played two different theaters in New Orleans that I can't remember the name and then we played a returning game and we played four different times and the closest I can remember that last time was around 1930s, the early 30s. I dare say, around about in the 31st, when I was down there that last time.
